body.target_estimand: \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pub}}(\Sigma)=\{\operatorname{sign}(B_{12}B_{21}):(B,\widetilde D)\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{pub}}(\Sigma)\}\), followed by the bounded-margin refinement \(\mathcal P(\Sigma)=\{\operatorname{sign}(A_{12}A_{21}):(A,D)\in\mathcal F(\Sigma)\}\).
body.estimand_functional: For every \(t\)-faithful covariance, \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{pub}}(\Sigma)=\{-1,+1\}\); for the bounded-margin refinement, \(\mathcal P(\Sigma)=\{+1:\text{a same-sign sector passes the finite certificate}\}\cup\{-1:\text{an opposite-sign sector passes the finite certificate}\}\).

sampling_model.design: Independent cross-sectional equilibrium sampling from \(dX_t=BX_t\,dt+\widetilde D^{1/2}dW_t\), equivalently \(dX_t=-AX_t\,dt+D^{1/2}dW_t\) after the common trace-one time gauge. The unrestricted published complete-two-cycle class is analyzed first; sampling guarantees concern the bounded-margin refinement.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the generator coefficients are \(-A_{12}\) and \(-A_{21}\), whose product has the same sign as \(A_{12}A_{21}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; strict diffusion positivity and covariance eigenvalue bounds replace treatment overlap.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The regular nuisance is \(\Sigma\), estimated by \(S_n\). Drift and diffusion are existentially profiled through the four sector certificates. In raw generator units the refinement requires \(|B_{12}|/\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\ge\eta\), \(|B_{21}|/\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\ge\eta\), and \(\lVert B\rVert_F/\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\le M\); covariance compactness through \(\kappa\) is used only for uniform inference.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The published model uses a Hurwitz generator, strictly positive diagonal diffusion, \(t\)-faithfulness, and structural minimality; its Theorem 4.2 characterizes ambiguity of one target edge.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Published-class polarity theorem and bounded-margin sector theorem

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Global drift identifiability with diagonal volatility holds exactly for simple graphs, and the directed two-cycle has a nontrivial Lyapunov fiber.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Affine-fiber lemma and published-class polarity theorem

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The Lyapunov trek rule yields a power-series covariance expansion and acyclic variance inequalities.
Model equivalence and structural identifiability are characterized for acyclic graphical continuous Lyapunov models.
An \(\ell_1\)-regularized Lyapunov estimator has model-selection guarantees under an irrepresentability condition.
Criterion inversion yields confidence regions, consistency, and rates for identified sets.
Directional differentiability determines when the standard bootstrap fails and supports locally valid alternatives.
Weakly regular parameters admit local impossibility results through underlying regular parameters.
Higher-order cumulant equations generically identify the drift under non-Gaussianity and support asymptotically normal estimation.

body.tldr: In the unrestricted published bivariate complete-two-cycle SCM, every \(t\)-faithful stationary covariance admits full-support Hurwitz generators of both cycle-product polarities, so Gaussian equilibrium snapshots never identify that product sign. The analyst-imposed refinement instead bounds the scale-invariant raw ratios \(|B_{12}|/\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\), \(|B_{21}|/\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\), and \(\lVert B\rVert_F/\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde D)\), represented after the trace-one gauge by \(\eta\) and \(M\). On that refinement, a complete four-sector certificate characterizes the compatible polarity set, including every strict-diffusion and norm-attainment branch, equal-variance thresholds, an asymmetric contact, honest covariance-region inversion, uniform singleton recovery beyond root-\(n\) clearance, and a matching local Gaussian obstruction.

project_justification.gap: The published bivariate complete-two-cycle class leaves a one-dimensional circulation fiber after covariance is fixed, but the consequence for the joint edge-product sign was not separated from individual-edge ambiguity. The first result closes that global question negatively: every \(t\)-faithful covariance admits both product polarities. Existing work also does not give the exact four-sector, open-versus-closed certificate obtained after imposing scale-invariant edge margins and a drift-norm cap, nor its contact-specific inference theory.
project_justification.niche: The exactly bivariate feedback cycle is the smallest graph where the unrestricted published SCM is globally product-sign nonidentifying yet an analyst's scientifically bounded refinement can identify a joint causal sign while neither individual edge sign is identified. Common rescaling of the raw generator and diffusion changes time units but leaves the stationary covariance and product polarity fixed, so the restrictions are formulated as raw trace ratios and computed in their unique trace-one representative.
project_justification.fill: The paper first constructs same-sign and opposite-sign full-support witnesses throughout the unrestricted \(t\)-faithful published class, proving that its compatible polarity set is always \(\{-1,+1\}\). It then derives the affine trace-normalized fiber and a complete finite semialgebraic certificate for the bounded-margin refinement, proves all strict-attainment branches, gives analytic equal-variance and asymmetric-contact reductions, exhibits an open \(t\)-faithful joint-only region, and propagates the population set through an honest Gaussian covariance confidence region with locally matching root-\(n\) limits.

body.related_work: Van Seeventer and Salehkaleybar (2026) formulate the published graphical continuous-Lyapunov class using a Hurwitz generator, strictly positive diagonal diffusion, \(t\)-faithfulness, and structural minimality, and their Theorem 4.2 and Remark 5.1 analyze one-edge sign ambiguity by linear feasibility. The present first theorem stays in that unrestricted class and proves a global negative result for the two-edge product: every \(t\)-faithful bivariate complete-cycle covariance admits both polarities. The later positive identification regions require the separately declared scale-invariant edge margins and drift-norm cap. Dettling, Homs, Améndola, Drton, and Hansen (2023) identify the directed two-cycle as the obstruction to global drift recovery with diagonal volatility; their Lyapunov rank analysis motivates, but does not provide, the polarity witnesses or strict-boundary certificate here. Hansen (2025) gives a trek expansion and acyclic variance inequalities. Dettling, Drton, and Kolar (2024) study penalized graph selection rather than inference on a known graph's compatible sign quotient. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) inform confidence-region inversion; Fang and Santos (2019) and Kaji (2021) inform nonsmooth and weak-identification comparisons. Recke and Hansen (2026) use non-Gaussian higher cumulants to recover information that is absent from the Gaussian snapshot experiment studied here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The equality-active certificate is complete on full-dimensional, line, point, dependent-row, strict-diffusion, and norm-equality branches, and the covariance inversion and local lower bound are proved. The remaining limitations are matters of declared scope rather than unresolved proof steps: the metric comparison and lower bound are local to compact regular contact subcharts.
body.honest_scope: The unrestricted headline applies only to the exactly bivariate, \(t\)-faithful, structurally minimal complete two-cycle with positive diagonal diffusion; it proves global nonidentification, not recovery. Singleton regions, equal-variance thresholds, contacts, and inference concern the analyst-imposed bounded-margin refinement expressed by raw trace ratios, with \(\kappa\) used for uniform covariance inference. The paper excludes larger-graph projection, marginalization, empirical-performance claims, and any global equivalence between certificate margin and covariance distance. Its distance equivalence and Gaussian lower bound are confined to compact regular subcharts of the explicit asymmetric contact.
